blocks.orig: One of the main reasons people travel to Tanzania is the chance to see the Big Five. Tanzania is one of the few places in Africa where you can see all five of them, in their natural habitat of course! In this blog, we tell you which parks to visit to see them all!
blocks.html: For many travellers, the chance to see the Big Five is a main reason to come to Tanzania. It is one of the few countries in Africa where all five can be seen, and in their natural habitat, naturally! This blog explains which parks you should visit to tick off every one of them.

blocks.orig: The term Big Five is used commonly and has been for a long time, but its background is less pleasant. It used to be very popular among hunters to shoot an animal from the Big Five. These would be the animals that are the most difficult to hunt. Fortunately, today these animals are not hunted anymore, and we only shoot beautiful photographs of them with a camera. Many tourists who come to Tanzania, want to shoot many beautiful photos of the Big Five animals as a memory to take home.
blocks.html: The phrase Big Five has been in common use for a long time, but its origins are less appealing. Among hunters it was once very popular to shoot one of the Big Five, as these were the animals considered hardest to hunt. Happily, these animals are no longer hunted today; the only shooting we do is taking beautiful photographs with a camera. Plenty of visitors to Tanzania want to bring home lots of fine photos of the Big Five as a lasting memory.

blocks.orig: Why is Tanzania the best destination to see the Big Five?
blocks.html: What makes Tanzania the best place to see the Big Five?

blocks.orig: Each animal lives in a certain environment. While in many other African countries it requires hard work to spot wildlife, it is somehow “easier” in Tanzania. This is because the concentration of wild animals in Tanzania is very high. Nature is still untouched and the conditions that the animals need are nowhere as good as in Tanzania. Your safari guide can tell you more about this during your safari.
blocks.html: Every animal has its own particular environment. In many other African countries spotting wildlife takes real effort, yet in Tanzania it is somehow “easier”. The reason is the very high density of wild animals here. Nature remains untouched, and nowhere else do the animals find the conditions they need as good as in Tanzania. Your safari guide will gladly explain more about this while you are on safari.

blocks.orig: See the animals in their natural habitat
blocks.html: Watch the animals in their own habitat

blocks.orig: While you are on safari in Tanzania, you see that this country gives you the real African safari experience because nature is still untouched. While tarmac roads have been built and fences have been placed around the parks in other countries, you will not encounter this in the Tanzanian national parks. This provides you with the ultimate safari feeling.
blocks.html: On safari in Tanzania you will notice that the country offers the genuine African safari experience, because nature has been left untouched. Elsewhere, tarmac roads have been laid and fences put up around the parks; in the Tanzanian national parks you will find none of that. The result is the ultimate safari feeling.

blocks.orig: The lion is perhaps the most popular animal of the Big Five. You can find lions in groups of up to 25 individuals. You can find lions in most Tanzanian national parks, and Tarangire National Park, Lake Manyara National Park, the Ngorongoro Crater and Serengeti National Park are no exception. The latter is the most famous national park in the world and is regarded as the best place to spot lions. Here you will find the highest concentration of big cats in the world. Besides lions, these are the leopard and the cheetah.
blocks.html: Of the Big Five, the lion is probably the best loved. Lions live in groups of up to 25 animals. They occur in most Tanzanian national parks, and Tarangire National Park, Lake Manyara National Park, the Ngorongoro Crater and Serengeti National Park are no exception. The Serengeti is the most famous national park on earth and is seen as the finest place to spot lions, with the highest concentration of big cats anywhere in the world. Alongside lions, these big cats are the leopard and the cheetah.

blocks.orig: A leopard is one of the more difficult Big Five animals to spot. They mostly sit in trees and often hunt either early morning or evening. When they catch their prey, they take it up a tree. Many confuse a leopard with a cheetah, however, a cheetah is smaller, slimmer and much faster. Also, cheetahs don’t climb trees, because they have no claws. You can spot leopards in the same national parks mentioned for lions.
blocks.html: The leopard is among the harder Big Five animals to find. Leopards spend much of their time in trees and tend to hunt in the early morning or evening. Once they have caught their prey, they haul it up into a tree. People often mix up leopards and cheetahs, but a cheetah is smaller, slimmer and a great deal faster. Cheetahs also don’t climb trees, as they lack claws. Leopards can be seen in the same national parks listed for lions.

blocks.orig: The elephant is a member of the Big Five that you can hardly miss in Tanzania. There are a lot of elephants in Tanzania. The best national park to spot elephants is Tarangire National Park. Here you can sometimes spot over a hundred elephants at once at the Tarangire River. Fortunately, the elephant population has grown in Tanzania over recent years. This is because illegal hunters are currently severely punished.
blocks.html: Elephants are one Big Five member you can hardly fail to see in Tanzania, as the country has a great many of them. The top national park for elephants is Tarangire National Park, where you can sometimes watch more than a hundred at once along the Tarangire River. Happily, Tanzania's elephant numbers have risen in recent years, because poachers now face severe punishment.

blocks.orig: The rhinoceros is the most difficult to spot. It is an endangered species and therefore very rarely seen. Rhinos can be found in both Serengeti National Park and the Ngorongoro Crater. Our customers mostly manage to spot the rhino in the crater, and the population is slowly growing in numbers. Again, because illegal hunting is severely punished, and the focus is on conservation rather than hunting these days.
blocks.html: The rhinoceros is the hardest of all to find. As an endangered species it is seen only very rarely. Rhinos live in both Serengeti National Park and the Ngorongoro Crater. Most of our customers who do see a rhino see it in the crater, and the population there is gradually increasing. Once again this is because poaching is punished harshly and the emphasis nowadays lies on conservation rather than hunting.

blocks.orig: The buffalo is a member of the Big Five that is easy to spot. It can be found in all Tanzanian national parks. Buffalos live in large groups. They are very strong and win fights with many predators, but as herbivores, they only eat grass.
blocks.html: The buffalo is the Big Five member that is simplest to spot, and it lives in every Tanzanian national park. Buffalos move in large herds. They are extremely strong and come out on top in fights with many predators, yet as herbivores they eat nothing but grass.
